utility.notes: Rhode Island Energy (a PPL Corporation subsidiary, formerly National Grid's Rhode Island electric/gas business) is the investor-owned utility serving Providence, directly confirmed via the utility's own site. Most Rhode Island municipalities are Rhode Island Energy territory; a small number (e.g. Burrillville's Pascoag/Clear River Electric & Water District, and Block Island) are served by separate municipal/cooperative utilities and are NOT assumed to be Rhode Island Energy territory.

value.name: Rhode Island Energy
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator or other separate generation supplier was found serving Providence this session; Rhode Island Energy is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

permit_authority.value: City of Providence Department of Inspection and Standards (DIS)
permit_authority.notes: Directly confirmed via the City's own site. DIS relocated to 780 Allens Avenue as of December 12, 2025.

interconnection_url.notes: Rhode Island Energy's own interconnection process page. Confirms a 'Simplified Interconnection Process' for small renewable systems using a single UL1741-listed inverter with aggregate DG size <=25kW AC — the typical residential rooftop solar case. This is a utility-wide process, not city-specific, and applies to every Rhode Island Energy-territory municipality.

value.name: Energy Storage Rebate (ESR) Program
value.administrator: Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources (OER)
value.description: Statewide rebate for behind-the-meter battery energy storage systems up to 250kW, funded by Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) proceeds. Tier 1 (<=25kW AC): $250/kWh base incentive ($8,000 project max) or $500/kWh income-eligible incentive ($16,000 project max), max rebate reached at 32kWh. Tier 2 (25-250kW AC): $175/kWh, $45,500 project max. Total program funding $2,000,000 ($1,300,000 Tier 1 / $700,000 Tier 2), first-come first-reserved. Eligible to property owners with an active account with Rhode Island Energy, Clear River Electric and Water (CREW) District, or Block Island Utility District — a genuinely statewide program, directly confirmed via OER's own program page.
value.eligibility: Property owner with an active electric account with Rhode Island Energy, Clear River Electric and Water District, or Block Island Utility District; new behind-the-meter grid-connected battery installation; installation agreement dated on or after the program's April 10 launch date; residential systems capped at 50kW AC (Tier 1 base rate applies up to 25kW AC).

battery_programs.notes: Directly confirmed via the Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources' own Energy Storage Rebates page this session. A statewide program applicable to every Rhode Island municipality served by an eligible utility, not city-specific — reused as a state-level fact per docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md's multi-state reuse rule. The page's 'launch date' is referenced as 'April 10' without an explicit year stated on the page; recorded as effective_from: null rather than guessed.

required_documents.notes: The City's official 'Checklist for Solar PV Installations' PDF exists but is a scanned/image-based document that could not be read this session; no other City page enumerated a solar-specific document checklist.

permit_fees.notes: Rhode Island's Building Code Commission (ribcc.ri.gov) and RI Dept. of State (rules.sos.ri.gov, 510-RICR-00-00-21) both reference a 'Statewide Permit Formula' governing municipal building-permit fees, but the exact formula/rate could not be independently read this session (dynamic page content did not render text via automated fetch), so no dollar figure is recorded.
